A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSG-12M and Poly2Graph work and contain 49 pages, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original GNN classification experiments in Section 4 and Table 2, supplementary measurements in Tables A5–A8, and Poly2Graph timing experiments in Appendix C.5 and Table A3.

after.justification: v5 retains the original classification, efficiency, and timing results in Table 2 and Tables A3 and A5–A8. These retained experiments qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The Poly2Graph procedure in Section 2 and Appendix C, including Algorithm 1, is unchanged. Root finding, adaptive refinement, skeleton extraction, post-processing, and the reference graph featurization remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five static HSG classification settings. Dataset construction and coverage are unchanged; T-HSG-5M remains a released temporal collection without dynamic-task benchmark results.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Tables A5–A8 retain GCN, GAT, GATv2, GIN, GINE, MF, CGCNN, and GraphSAGE. The timing comparison in Table A3 also retains the same code from Tai and Lee (2023) as its comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E retains the same preprocessing, stratified 8:1:1 splits, evaluation metrics, batch size of 6000, and training caps of 100 epochs and 1000 steps. Model configurations and parameter-matching controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or case study is added or removed. The illustrated component-fragmentation cases in Figure A4 and the other spectral-graph examples are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 42, 2025, and 666 in Appendix E.2 and report benchmark means and standard deviations over three seeds. Uncertainty reporting in Table A3 is also unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and reported findings in Table 2 and Tables A3 and A5–A8 are identical. For example, GraphSAGE retains HSG-12M accuracy of 0.546 ± 0.004 and Top-10 accuracy of 0.952 ± 0.001 under the same settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Appendix B, companion-matrix construction in Appendix C, and Toeplitz-decomposition argument in Appendix F are unchanged. No formal assumption, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about automated spectral-graph extraction, dataset scale and novelty, graph-learning challenges, and spectral fingerprints for algebraic objects.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning edge geometry, GraphSAGE performance under limited budgets, and inverse-design potential are unchanged. Appendices C.6 and H retain the same fragmentation, representation, benchmark, and temporal-modeling limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, licenses, code and dataset access information, and the Appendix G tutorial are unchanged. The added author email does not revise technical documentation or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with existing graph datasets and discussions of spatial multigraph learning and non-Bloch theory in Appendices A and D.

P1.justification: v5 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and Xianquan Yan's correspondence email, with adjusted author footnote symbols and an updated arXiv stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added header and author footnote produce limited presentation changes. One introduction line moves from page 1 to page 2, slightly shifting Figure 1. Figure and table designs are unchanged; pages 3–49 render identically below the new header.

improvement.justification: v5 updates publication and contact metadata with minor opening-page reflow. The scientific content, empirical evidence, theory, reproducibility documentation, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These administrative edits do not materially improve or harm the paper's overall quality.
